statement-with-continuation.comment: A statement whose first line ends in a trailing '\' (see indent-parser/src/tokenizer.ts): the block spans every physically-continued line, applying the normal attribute/string/etc. patterns to each, until a line is reached that does not itself end in '\'. Must come before #statement-keyword so a plain single-line statement isn't matched first. `end` is zero-width, anchored at the START of a line via lookahead rather than at true end-of-line via lookbehind: a lookbehind-anchored `(?<!\\)$` end pattern triggers a vscode-textmate/oniguruma engine quirk where inner `patterns` silently stop being applied on subsequent lines -- this lookahead form does not.

line-continuation.comment: A trailing '\' joins this line with the next physical line (see indent-parser/src/tokenizer.ts). TextMate can't actually join lines, so this just gives the marker itself a visible color instead of leaving it unclassified.
line-continuation.name: constant.character.escape.indent

statement-keyword.comment: The leading bareword/tag of a line, e.g. "org", "service", "->", "=>", ">=<", "!include" (a built-in directive kind; the leading '!' marks any current or future directive, e.g. a future "!schema"). Matched only at the true start of a line (after any leading indentation), mirroring the tree-sitter grammar's `type` rule. Excludes a leading ";" so full-line comments are left to the #comment pattern instead. The `\S+` match already covers a leading '!' with no charset change needed. Uses a lookbehind for the leading whitespace (`(?<=^\s*)`) instead of consuming it directly: consuming it would make this match start at column 0, which is earlier than #attribute's match (naturally starting after the whitespace) and would always win regardless of list order -- using a lookbehind keeps both patterns tied at the same start column so declaration order decides. Listed BEFORE #attribute so kind tokens containing a literal '=' (e.g. ">=<") are matched whole as a keyword instead of #attribute partially matching a leading fragment up to the '=' (e.g. misparsing ">=<" as attribute name ">" + '=' operator, leaving the trailing '<' unstyled).

attribute.comment: A `key=` attribute name immediately followed by the '=' operator. The value itself is left to the string/number/boolean patterns.
